title: Distributed agent cache
objection: A cache is easy. A cache that survives 200 concurrent misses on the same key is not.

claims.claim: 200 concurrent workers missed the same key → the model was called 1 time(s), not 200
claims.detail: 1 computed, 199 waited on the lease, 0 lease timeouts. Without a lease this is 200 model calls — a 200× bill and a rate-limit incident.

claims.claim: all 200 workers got a value back
claims.detail: p50 174.853 ms · p99 176.485 ms · wall 178 ms for the whole fan-in

claims.claim: a worker that dies holding the lease does not wedge the key — recovered in 2 ms
claims.detail: the lease has a TTL, so the next caller takes over rather than waiting forever

claims.claim: semantic tier caught 200/200 paraphrased prompts that an exact-key cache would have missed entirely
claims.detail: exact-key hit rate on paraphrased traffic is 0 by construction — this is the tier that pays for itself

claims.claim: 0/100 unrelated prompts were wrongly served from cache
claims.detail: threshold 0.92 — tune it against your own traffic; too low serves the wrong answer confidently

claims.claim: cached entry costs 95 B vs 1634 B for a key-per-entry cache (17.1×)
claims.detail: 1293 B payload · sharded hash + HEXPIRE + zstd, vs one string key per entry with EXPIRE
